## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/setup-linux-playwright.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
runtime="$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright"
/usr/bin/time -p mkdir -p "$runtime/output"
# Bound mirror stalls, including apt calls launched by Playwright's dependency installer.
/usr/bin/time -p sudo -n tee /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/80omgithub-network >/dev/null <<'APT'
Acquire::ForceIPv4 "true";
Acquire::Retries "1";
Acquire::http::Timeout "20";
Acquire::https::Timeout "20";
APT
/usr/bin/time -p timeout --kill-after=10s 180s sudo -n apt-get update
/usr/bin/time -p sudo -n apt-get install -y mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-tools xvfb xauth lsof
/usr/bin/time -p npm install --prefix "$runtime" --no-save --no-package-lock @playwright/cli@0.1.19 playwright
/usr/bin/time -p "$runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright" install --with-deps chromium
/usr/bin/time -p tee "$runtime/linux.json" >/dev/null <<JSON
{
  "outputDir": "$runtime/output",
  "browser": {
    "browserName": "chromium",
    "launchOptions": {
      "channel": "chromium",
      "headless": false,
      "args": ["--enable-gpu", "--ignore-gpu-blocklist", "--enable-unsafe-webgpu", "--use-angle=vulkan", "--enable-features=Vulkan", "--use-vulkan=swiftshader", "--use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader", "--disable-vulkan-surface"]
    }
  }
}
JSON
# Keep one display alive across CLI calls and fresh SSH shells.
if [[ ! -s "$runtime/display" ]] || ! kill -0 "$(cat "$runtime/xvfb.pid" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null; then
  : > "$runtime/display"
  /usr/bin/time -p bash -c 'nohup Xvfb -displayfd 3 -screen 0 1440x900x24 -nolisten tcp 3>"$1/display" >"$1/xvfb.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$1/xvfb.pid"' _ "$runtime"
  /usr/bin/time -p timeout 15 bash -c 'until test -s "$1/display"; do sleep 0.1; done' _ "$runtime"
fi
node_dir="$(dirname "$(command -v node)")"
/usr/bin/time -p cp "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/wip-screenshots.cjs" "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/wip-screenshot-hook.cjs" "$runtime/"
/usr/bin/time -p tee "$runtime/playwright-cli" >/dev/null <<WRAPPER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export PATH="$node_dir:\$PATH"
export DISPLAY=":\$(cat "$runtime/display")"
export PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR="$runtime/output"
export OMGITHUB_CAPTURE_WEB_DIR="${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:-}"
export OMGITHUB_PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT="$runtime"
export NODE_OPTIONS="--require=$runtime/wip-screenshot-hook.cjs \${NODE_OPTIONS:-}"
for arg in "\$@"; do
  case "\$arg" in
    -*) continue ;;
    open) exec "$runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright-cli" "\$@" --config "$runtime/linux.json" ;;
    *) break ;;
  esac
done
exec "$runtime/node_modules/.bin/playwright-cli" "\$@"
WRAPPER
/usr/bin/time -p chmod 755 "$runtime/playwright-cli"
/usr/bin/time -p sudo -n ln -sfn "$runtime/playwright-cli" /usr/local/bin/playwright-cli
if [[ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ]]; then
  /usr/bin/time -p printf '%s\n' /usr/local/bin >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
fi
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/local/bin/playwright-cli --version

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D one-room Zelda-style dungeon game with a key and a boss, optimized for phone/tablet, using a polished custom visual/audio presentation.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make and briefly note reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (`.jpg`, viewport max 1280px wide) for self-checks, reading only the latest; use full-size PNG only for fine detail.
- Support mobile touch controls and responsive layouts.
- One room, a key, and a boss.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JS Canvas 2D implementation; no framework or runtime dependencies.
- Original art direction: "Emberfall Vault", dark torch-lit stone chamber, golden ember magic, teal/orange knight, giant Cinder Warden boss.
- Game loop: find key in reliquary chest, use it to break seal, fight 3-phase boss.
- Boss patterns: slam shockwaves, charge, fire volley, fissure hazards; adds wisps and heart drops at phase changes.
- Touch: virtual joystick + slash/dodge/use buttons; keyboard WASD/arrows, J/Slash, Space/Shift dodge, E use.
- Downloaded OFL Google Fonts locally into `assets/`.
- Added debug API under `?debug` as `window.__emberfall` for forcing progression/state during testing.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built full playable game structure: title screen, HUD, objective, health, key indicator, boss bar, toast, interact prompts, victory/death screens, replay.
- Implemented player movement, sword combat, dodge, damage/invulnerability, chest/key interaction, gate unlock, boss AI/projectiles/shockwaves/hazards/wisps/pickups, win/loss flow.
- Implemented procedural audio engine, mute toggle, particles, screen shake, ambient embers, lighting.
- Implemented responsive layout, touch joystick/buttons, mobile CSS, safe-area padding.
- Added font files, favicon, local dev server running in tmux on port 3000.
- Extensive visual iteration: flagstone floor, central runner, raised boss dais, banners, chains, rubble/bones, barrier redesign, chest/pots/player art, boss art.
- Multiple desktop screenshots captured and reviewed.

### Active
- Visual polish pass after latest boss/cape/axe/head edits; latest edits not yet screenshotted/verified.
- Boss still reads somewhat "cute/robot-like"; current effort is making its silhouette more menacing with larger horns, spiked pauldrons, ragged cape, and single-bladed great axe.
- Need verify latest barrier "tangible sheet" and title layout changes.
- Need mobile/tablet viewport screenshots and touch-control verification.
- Need end-to-end gameplay test (movement, chest interaction, gate unlock, boss fight, victory/death).
- Performance is very poor under Playwright SwiftShader (~2–5 FPS); optimize static scene caching / effects, but real hardware likely much faster.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Reload and screenshot latest title, idle gameplay, boss-active, and boss phase attacks at 1280x800 JPEG; visually inspect and iterate.
2. Verify the latest boss redesign and barrier sheet actually render well and are not clipped.
3. Add local dark backdrop behind title content to stop the barrier beam crossing `VAULT`; increase right-side scene visibility if needed.
4. Test mobile portrait (e.g. 390x844) and tablet (e.g. 768x1024), including touch control layout and playability.
5. Test full progression: move to chest, use E, collect key, unlock gate, fight boss, trigger victory and death/replay.
6. Improve performance with static background/wall scene caching and lower-cost effects if needed.
7. Remove or gate profiling instrumentation/query flags (`?prof`, `?skip`, `?res`) or leave harmless; clean up obsolete screenshots.
8. Final check with `capture.sh`/Playwright and concise completion note listing assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: game DOM, overlays, HUD, title/end screens.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: responsive UI, title, HUD, touch controls, animations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: all gameplay, rendering, audio, responsive logic, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/`: local Cinzel/Spectral fonts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest visual checks (`title.jpg`, `play_idle.jpg`, `bossfight.jpg`, `cropboss.png`).
- `/tmp/opencode/shotj.mjs`: 1280x800 title JPEG capture helper.
- `/tmp/opencode/shotplay2.mjs`: start + idle/boss progression screenshot helper.
- `/tmp/opencode/shotboss2.mjs`: force boss-active screenshot helper.
- `/tmp/opencode/debugcheck.mjs`: verifies debug API and state transitions.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`: static server entrypoint used by `start.sh`.

## Important Context
- Dev server running via tmux session `game`: `PORT=3000 node /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-start.mjs`; URL `http://localhost:3000`.
- Playwright CLI initially lacked matching Chromium; ran `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.
- `playwright-cli screenshot` timed out at 5s due low FPS; use direct Playwright Node scripts with `timeout: 60000` and JPEG output.
- Screenshot helper pattern: launch Chromium with `linux.json` launch options, set `DISPLAY` from runtime `display` file, screenshot at 1280x800 quality 85–90.
- `window.__emberfall` exists only with `?debug`; exposes `G`, `startGame`, `resetRun`, `startUnlock`, `grantKey`, `beginBossAwake`, `beginPhase`, `damageBoss`, `hurtPlayer`, `tryInteract`, `showEnd`, `spawnWisp`, `render`.
- To force boss fight in tests: set chest/key state, `grantKey()`, gate open, `progress='boss'`, call `beginBossAwake()`, force `boss.state='chase'`, add `boss-ui.show` class.

- Latest boss art code changes (scale `BS=clamp(base/720,.62,.94)`, larger head, spiked pauldrons, new single-blade axe) have not been visually verified.
- Game currently uncommitted in git; no commit/push performed.

input.newString:
# Emberfall Vault

A complete one-room Zelda-style dungeon built with plain HTML, CSS, and Canvas 2D. No frameworks, no build step, no runtime dependencies.

- **Objective:** find the Ember Key in the reliquary, break the seal, and defeat Morgrave, the Cinder Warden.
- **The fight:** three phases with slam shockwaves, charges, fire volleys, fissures, and summoned embers.
- **Controls (desktop):** `WASD`/arrows move, `J` slash, `Space`/`Shift` dodge, `E` interact, `M` mute.
- **Controls (touch):** virtual stick on the left; slash, dodge, and use buttons on the right.
- **Presentation:** procedural art and audio, torch-lit stone chamber, responsive layout for phone, tablet, and desktop.

Run `./start.sh` (or serve the folder with any static server) and open `index.html`. Add `?debug` to expose the `window.__emberfall` test hooks.

All art, fonts, and audio are bundled locally. Fonts: Cinzel and Spectral (SIL Open Font License).
